About Me

A first-year at IIT Bombay who’s curious about a lot of things.

Hey, I’m Atharva

I’m a first-year B.Tech student in Electrical Engineering at IIT Bombay, currently based in Mumbai. This page is the long version of who I am: where I started, how I got here, and what I get up to when I’m not studying.

Right now

I joined IIT Bombay in July 2026 and I’m in my first year of Electrical Engineering. Everything’s still new, and I’m taking it one step at a time.

01 · The beginning

How it all started

Maths and science have fascinated me since I was a kid. Olympiads were where that curiosity first got room to stretch, and the IOQM (Indian Olympiad Qualifier in Mathematics) is the one that really hooked me. I found it fascinating, and it pulled me into the science olympiads next.

After that, JEE became the next big goal, and that road is what eventually led me to IIT Bombay.

03 · Proud moment

Cracking JEE

Two years of rigorous prep, and it paid off: AIR 299 in JEE Advanced, which is what got me into IIT Bombay. It’s the thing I’m proudest of so far.

05 · Looking ahead

What I’m after

Where I want to be

I want to see myself doing the work I love. I haven’t locked into one path yet, and I’m fine with that.

What I care about

Happiness. It’s what I keep coming back to: I want the work I do, and the life around it, to make me happy.

Projects

Things I've built, with what worked and what I learned.

Tilt-steered robotic car with autonomous navigation

XLR8, Electronics and Robotics Club, IIT Bombay · August 2026
Raspberry Pi Pico WMPU-6050 IMUESP-01Ultrasonic sensorServo
  • Built for IIT Bombay's flagship robotics competition, which needed a custom-steered car to cross a 40 cm wide obstacle-filled track within a set time.
  • Designed and made the chassis and suspension, with manual steering that reads tilt from the IMU. A servo-mounted ultrasonic sensor handles obstacle detection when the bot is out of the driver's line of sight.
  • Went from concept to a working prototype in 10 days, and cleared 9 of 13 obstacles in the final run within 12 minutes.
  • It was my first engineering project: ten days of late nights debugging circuits and reworking the mechanical design.
